punchline: Marcus Aurelius told himself: take away the complaint "I have been harmed", and the harm is gone.
thirty_sec: Marcus Aurelius admits in his notebook that he longs for retreats, houses in the country, sea-shores, mountains. Then he tells himself the best retreat is his own mind. Elsewhere he writes that when something outside hurts him, it isn't the thing that disturbs him but his own judgement about it, and that he can wipe that judgement out right now. He was running a war when he wrote it.
